arxiv-2110-12363.title: Robust Sliding Mode Control of a Magnetic Levitation System: Continuous-Time and Discrete-Time Approaches
arxiv-2110-12363.creator: Pratik Vernekar, Vitthal Bandal
arxiv-2110-12363.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Pratik Vernekar, Vitthal Bandal. This paper presents three types of sliding mode controllers for a magnetic levitation system. First, a proportional-integral sliding mode controller (PI-SMC) is designed using a new switching surface and a proportional plus power rate reaching law. The PI-SMC is more robust than a feedback linearization controller in the presence of mismatched uncertainties and outperforms the SMC schemes reported recently in the literature in terms of the convergence rate and settling time.

arxiv-2210-13442.title: Protocols for classically training quantum generative models on probability distributions
arxiv-2210-13442.creator: Sachin Kasture, Oleksandr Kyriienko, Vincent E. Elfving
arxiv-2210-13442.description: Abstract Quantum Generative Modelling (QGM) relies on preparing quantum states and generating samples from these states as hidden — or known — probability distributions. As distributions from some classes of quantum states (circuits) are inherently hard to sample classically, QGM represents an excellent testbed for quantum supremacy experiments.

arxiv-2303-13890.title: Regularity and asymptotics of densities of inverse subordinators
arxiv-2303-13890.creator: Giacomo Ascione 1, Mladen Savov 2,3, Bruno Toaldo 4
arxiv-2303-13890.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Giacomo Ascione 1, Mladen Savov 2,3, Bruno Toaldo 4. In this article densities (and their derivatives) of subordinators and inverse subordinators are considered. Under minor restrictions, generally milder than the existing in the literature, employing a useful modification of the saddle point method, we obtain the large asymptotic behaviour of these densities (and their derivatives) for a specific region of space and time and quantify how the ratio between time and space affects the explicit speed of convergence.

arxiv-2402-03835.title: Transformer based Endmember Fusion with Spatial Context for Hyperspectral Unmixing
arxiv-2402-03835.creator: R. M. K. L. Ratnayake, D. M. U. P. Sumanasekara, H. M. K. D. Wickramathilaka, G. M. R. I. Godaliyadda, M. P. B. Ekanayake, H. M. V. R. Herath
arxiv-2402-03835.description: Abstract In recent years, transformer-based deep learning networks have gained popularity in Hyperspectral (HS) unmixing applications due to their superior performance. The attention mechanism within transformers facilitates input-dependent weighting and enhances contextual awareness during training. Drawing inspiration from this, we propose a novel attention-based Hyperspectral Unmixing algorithm called Transformer-based Endmember Fusion with Spatial Context for Hyperspectral Unmixing (FusionNet) .

arxiv-2405-19875.description: Abstract . Recently, it was shown that the image of a Toeplitz kernel of dimension greater than 1 1 under composition by an inner function is nearly S ∗ S^{*} -invariant if and only if the inner function is an automorphism.

arxiv-2407-09991.title: Threshold photo-production of J / Ψ J/\Psi off light nuclei
arxiv-2407-09991.creator: Fangcheng He, Ismail Zahed
arxiv-2407-09991.description:
A 2024 arXiv research paper by Fangcheng He, Ismail Zahed. We analyze threshold photoproduction of heavy mesons off a deuteron and Helium-4, using the QCD factorization method. Assuming large skewness, the production amplitude is dominated by the leading twist-2 gluonic energy-momentum tensor (EMT). We use our recent results for the gluonic gravitational form factors of light nuclei in the impulse approximation, to estimate the differential cross sections for J / Ψ J/\Psi production off a deuteron and Helium-4 at current electron facilities. arxiv-2412-21018.title: Unified structures for solutions of Painlevé equation II.
arxiv-2412-21018.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by . We present certain general structures related to the solutions of Painlevé equation II and to the solutions of the differential equation satisfied by the corresponding Hamiltonian equations, together with the tau functions. By taking advantage of the Bäcklund transformations we find a linear differential equation satisfied by the tau functions and explicit rational expressions linking the solutions of Painlevé equation II, Painlevé equation XXXIV and the Hamiltonians with the tau functions. Also, recursions for the tau functions and the Hamiltonians will be given.

arxiv-2504-01908.title: Benchmarking Synthetic Tabular Data: A Multi-Dimensional Evaluation Framework
arxiv-2504-01908.creator: Andrey Sidorenko, Michael Platzer, Mario Scriminaci, Paul Tiwald
arxiv-2504-01908.description: Abstract Evaluating the quality of synthetic data remains a key challenge for ensuring privacy and utility in data-driven research. In this work, we present an evaluation framework that quantifies how well synthetic data replicates original distributional properties while ensuring privacy.

arxiv-2512-12714.title: Delta operation at height 2
arxiv-2512-12714.creator: Noam Nissan
arxiv-2512-12714.description: Abstract We compute the delta power operation for morava E-theory of height 2 at the prime 3. The delta power operation was defined using the notion of higher semi additivity by Shachar Carmeli, Tomer M. Schlank and Lior Yanovski. We briefly survey the basic definitions in higher semi-additivity.

arxiv-2602-13397.title: Revising the Milky Way Cepheid Calibration: Quantifying and Correcting for Previously Undetected Distance Modulus Errors in the Gaia-based Multi-Wavelength Period-Luminosity Relations.
arxiv-2602-13397.creator: Barry F. Madore, Wendy L. Freedman
arxiv-2602-13397.description: Abstract We examine the multi-wavelength period–luminosity–color (PLC) relations for Cepheid variables in the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds and the Milky Way. From first-principles stellar physics, the luminosity of a Cepheid is determined by its radius and surface temperature, yielding a fundamental PLC relation whose observational proxies are pulsation period and intrinsic color.

pmc-11644909.title: Improving the Calibration of Low-Cost Sensors Using Data Assimilation
pmc-11644909.creator: Diego Alberto Aranda Britez, Alejandro Tapia Córdoba, Princy Johnson, Erid Eulogio Pacheco Viana, Pablo Millán Gata, Carlos Campillo
pmc-11644909.description: In the context of smart agriculture, accurate soil moisture monitoring is crucial to optimise irrigation, improve water usage efficiency and increase crop yields. Although low-cost capacitive sensors are used to make monitoring affordable, these sensors face accuracy challenges that often result in inefficient irrigation practices. This paper presents a method for calibrating capacitive soil moisture sensors through data assimilation.

pmc-12790197.title: Multiple Left Ventricular Ball Thrombi in a Patient With Nonischemic Cardiomyopathy Bridged to Heart-Lung Transplantation
pmc-12790197.creator: Adam Zviman, Julie Zviman, Sarah Cipriano, Allen Burke, Manjula Ananthram
pmc-12790197.description: Case SummaryWe present a case of a young patient with a history of recurrent venous thromboembolism, stroke status post fibrinolysis, and titin-related dilated cardiomyopathy who developed cardiogenic shock in the setting of decompensated heart failure and concomitant large left ventricular thrombus comprising ∼75% of the cavity. Her shock was managed medically as she was evaluated for surgical heart failure therapies.
